title: Start with the whole system
subtitle: Six layers. One laptop. A clear place for every change.
quiz: Where should your personal documents be represented?
As Nix strings in flake.nix
As persistent data with separate backups
As packages in Nixpkgs
Nix describes how the system is assembled. Documents remain mutable data and need persistence plus backups.

title: Read the Nix language
subtitle: Recognize the small patterns used throughout this repository.
quiz: What does app.origin or "flathub" do?
Combines two origins
Uses flathub when origin is missing
Runs a shell command
The 'or' syntax supplies an attribute-selection fallback.

title: Modules, options & merging
subtitle: A file being present is not enough. It must be imported.
quiz: You create a new service module. What makes it part of Shadow?
Its filename
Including it through the host’s import graph
Restarting your editor
A module contributes only when the configuration imports it.

title: Flakes, locks & trust
subtitle: Where software comes from, and what an update really changes.
quiz: Does updating flake.lock switch your operating system?
Yes, immediately
No; build and activation are separate
Only if the file is staged
Updating records new dependency revisions. The running system changes through activation.

title: Check → build → test → switch
subtitle: Know exactly which command can change the running machine.
quiz: Which action checks your system without activating it?
sys-switch
sys-test
sys-build
Build realizes the system. Test and Switch both activate it.

title: Where to add something
subtitle: Choose the owner before choosing the file.
quiz: Where should a particular project’s Node.js version go?
Its devenv configuration
The laptop’s global package list
The firewall module
Project-local toolchains prevent unrelated projects from sharing an accidental global version.

title: Add & manage a Flatpak
subtitle: One catalog entry, three derived behaviors.
quiz: Why do theme extensions use persist = false?
Their code is insecure
They have no per-app data to preserve
It disables their updates
Persistence controls saved application data, not update behavior or trust.

title: Understand app permissions
subtitle: A sandbox is a set of capabilities, not a single security switch.
quiz: Does !home remove every Documents grant inherited from an app?
Yes
No; narrower filesystem grants can remain
Only for native apps
Broad path denial and a reset of inherited filesystem grants are different policies.

title: What survives a reboot
subtitle: A temporary root does not make your retained data temporary.
quiz: You save a valuable file in Downloads, then reboot. What should you expect?
It is always backed up
It may be lost; Downloads is not preserved
Nix copies it into the store
Move valuable files to Documents or another retained directory before reboot.

title: Every key has a different job
subtitle: Stop treating disk, age, VPN, SSH, and signing keys as the same thing.
quiz: You add another VPN provider. Do you normally need a fresh age identity?
Yes, one for every app
No, encrypt its configuration to existing recipients
No, put its private key in flake.nix
age protects stored credentials; WireGuard authenticates the tunnel. Their identities have different jobs.

title: Add, deploy & rotate a secret
subtitle: Ciphertext in Git. Plaintext only where its consumer needs it.
quiz: Does encrypting a leaked token make the leaked copy invalid?
Yes
No; rotate or revoke it at the provider
Only after reboot
Encryption protects stored copies. Provider-side rotation invalidates exposed credentials.

title: DNS, VPN & the firewall
subtitle: Different layers protect different parts of a connection.
quiz: Does an inbound firewall stop every app from contacting the internet?
Yes
No; outbound policy is a different concern
Only when a VPN is active
The configured inbound firewall controls incoming reachability, not a per-app outbound domain policy.

title: Add & operate a VPN
subtitle: Connect encrypted credentials to a real connection controller.
quiz: What proves a tunnel is leak-free?
The VPN icon is visible
Explicit routing/DNS/IPv6 and failure tests
The config is encrypted
Encryption at rest and an active interface do not establish the actual packet path.

title: Security without magic labels
subtitle: Understand what each protection covers—and what it cannot cover.
quiz: Does AppArmor enablement prove all apps are confined?
Yes
No; enforced profiles and covered processes matter
Only for Flatpak
The security module must have applicable enforced policies; enablement alone is not coverage.

title: Project environments & editors
subtitle: Your laptop supplies orchestration; each project supplies its toolchain.
quiz: Why preserve direnv approvals?
To approve future changes automatically
To retain approval of unchanged reviewed .envrc content
To disable its trust check
Approval is content-based. Changed files still require review and approval.

title: Recovery, backups & cleanup
subtitle: Configurations roll back. Data needs another copy.
quiz: Your password database is accidentally deleted. Which mechanism can restore its contents?
A verified data backup
Changing flake.lock
A package-generation rollback alone
A configuration generation does not contain your mutable password database.

title: Find the cause of a failure
subtitle: Separate evaluation, build, activation, and runtime errors.
quiz: A tool cannot open the user D-Bus socket. What does that prove?
The keyring is absent
Only that this tool could not reach that socket
The VPN is disconnected
Test from the relevant session before concluding a service is absent.
